Effective line: Shh. Keep it down. Old Fern. Composter.
Suggested line: Keep your voice down, will you? I'm Old Fern. Composter, which in this city is about the worst thing a person can be.

Effective line: I turned this city's waste back into soil. Now that's 'untidy', and so am I. Criminally untidy. Worms in my hat to prove it.
Suggested line: I spent forty years turning this city's scraps back into soil, and now that's 'untidy'. So am I, apparently. I've got worms in my hat to prove it.

Effective line: They shoved the rubbish behind the facade and called it 'Behind'. The land's sick. Nothing grows. Help me save what's left.
Suggested line: They swept the rubbish behind the facade and pretended it wasn't there. Now the soil's sick, nothing grows in the Reek, and I'm too old to dig alone. Help me save what's left.

Effective line: Any luck? The heaps are in cellars and holes all over the Reek. They think they're hiding. They're being rescued.
Suggested line: Any luck? The heaps are tucked into cellars and holes all over the Reek. They think they're hiding from the inspectors. Tell them they're coming home.

Effective line: Oh. A visitor. Forgive me, I've forgotten how this goes. I am Widow Pell. My husband died three years ago, in his chair in the front parlour.
Suggested line: Oh, you've come to the door. Forgive me, it's been a long while since anyone did. I'm Widow Pell. My husband died three years ago, in his chair in the front parlour.

Effective line: I cannot bury him. Form 27-B needs Form 27-C, and 27-C needs 27-B. He has waited in his chair for three years.
Suggested line: And I can't bury him. Form 27-B needs a 27-C, and the 27-C needs a 27-B, so he's still in his chair, waiting, the way he always used to wait for me.

Effective line: I talk to him in the parlour. He was always the patient one. I'm not, it turns out. Please, if you can help.
Suggested line: I still talk to him in there. He was always the patient one of us, and it turns out I'm not. If you can help at all, please.

Effective line: The stamp, remember. Someone hid the Stamp of Final Approval where nobody official would look: somewhere in Grave Row, among papers nobody reads.
Suggested line: Someone hid the Stamp of Final Approval where no official would ever look: in Grave Row, north of the permit office, among papers nobody reads.

Effective line: Rollo Spokes... foreman. Beefcake. Learned the wheels... in the Gainlands. Back then, a wheel stopped at night.
Suggested line: Name's Rollo Spokes... wheel foreman, Beefcake, out of the Gainlands. Back home... a wheel stopped at night... and so did the man on it.

Effective line: Now the facade needs light... so we pedal. Free. Forever. We were told... it was cardio. My calves have calves.
Suggested line: Here, the facade needs lighting... so we pedal it. No pay, no end. They told us it was cardio... My calves have calves.

Effective line: My crews run six hours a day... for ten years. Nobody's told them they can stop. Somebody ought to.
Suggested line: My crews have pedalled six hours a day for ten years... and nobody's ever told them they can stop. Somebody ought to... somebody they'll believe.

Effective line: Three wheels... pull the brakes. And that big cable by the east wall... feeds the facade. Cut it.
Suggested line: Three wheels in the Yards... pull each brake and talk to the crew. Then the big cable by the east wall, the one that feeds the facade... cut it.

Effective line: The crews won't stop... till somebody says it's all right. You say it.
Suggested line: The crews won't get off... till somebody tells them it's all right to. So you tell them... and mean it.

Effective line: Hands where I can see them. Good. Chef Marlo. Once of the Market of the Four Paths. Now a 'Nutrient Distributor'. Recipes stay in my apron.
Suggested line: Hands where I can see them... good, no inspector's gloves. I'm Chef Marlo. I cooked at the Market of the Four Paths, once. Now I'm a 'Nutrient Distributor', and my recipes stay in my apron.

Effective line: Three recipe cards, hidden in the quarter. And the dispenser: give it a good kick from me. Spoil it. Spoil it badly.
Suggested line: Three recipe cards, tucked away around the quarter, and then the dispenser. Spoil it for me, and spoil it badly. I've waited ten years to say that.

Effective line: Entry requires the Approved Visitor Standard. You are too tall. You are too short. Your shadow is the wrong length.
Suggested line: Entry requires the Approved Visitor Standard. You are somehow both too tall and too short, and your shadow is the wrong length.

Effective line: However. The Standard has a provision: the Entry Examination. A card battle. Win it, and you are, retroactively, approved.
Suggested line: However, the Standard provides for an Entry Examination, conducted as a card battle. Win it, and you are retroactively approved.

Effective line: You again. Still too tall. Still smiling at the wrong angle. Ready for the Examination?
Suggested line: You again, still too tall and still smiling at the wrong angle. Are you ready for the Examination?

Effective line: I have measured twelve thousand visitors. I approved four. Nine thousand were sent home. The rest, I will not say.
Suggested line: I have measured twelve thousand visitors and approved four. Nine thousand were sent home. About the rest, I would rather not say.

Effective line: Height inspection! Stand against the post. Straighten.
Suggested line: Height inspection! Stand against the post, please, and straighten up.

Effective line: Not that straight. Hm. You are one hair above regulation.
Suggested line: Not that straight. Hm... you are one hair above regulation.

Effective line: One hair. I will let it go. This time. Do not grow.
Suggested line: One hair, I will let go, this time. Please do not grow while you are inside.

Effective line: Queue management. The approved queue is this queue. You are in it.
Suggested line: Queue management! This is the approved queue, and you are already in it.

Effective line: Exit control. You are leaving? You have not arrived. Please arrive first.
Suggested line: Exit control. You wish to leave? But you have not finished arriving. Please arrive first.

Effective line: Exit control. Please have your exit permit ready. Please have your exit interview permit ready. Please have a reason.
Suggested line: Exit control. Please have your exit permit ready, and your exit interview permit, and, if at all possible, a reason.

Effective line: Citizen 4471. I smiled incorrectly. Eleven degrees. The approved angle is eight.
Suggested line: I am Citizen 4471. I was brought here for smiling incorrectly. Eleven degrees, when the approved angle is eight.

Effective line: It was my wife's wedding. I had been crying. They corrected me.
Suggested line: It was our wedding day. I had been crying, the happy kind, and they corrected me for that too.

Effective line: I do not smile any more. Not at all. It is a strange thing, to forget how a face works.
Suggested line: I do not smile at all any more. It is a strange thing, to forget how your own face works.

Effective line: Please. A burial permit is all we want: Form 27-B/6, stamped Final Approval.
Suggested line: All we want is a burial permit: Form 27-B/6, stamped Final Approval, and then he can finally rest.

Effective line: Somebody hid the Stamp of Final Approval in Grave Row, among papers nobody reads. Find it, bring it to our family plot at the north end of Grave Row, and let him rest.
Suggested line: Somebody hid the Stamp of Final Approval in Grave Row, north of the permit office, among papers nobody reads. Find it, take it to our family plot at the north end of the Row, and let him rest.

Effective line: The stamp is somewhere in Grave Row, among papers nobody reads. Then the plot, at the north end of the Row. Please.
Suggested line: The stamp's in Grave Row, north of the permit office, among papers nobody reads. Then bring it to our plot at the north end of the Row. Please.

Effective line: Here. This was his. He'd want a young person to have it.
Suggested line: Here, this was his. He'd want it to go to someone young, who'll use it.

Effective line: And something about the man in the castle. He schedules grief. Thursdays, 3:00 to 3:05. Anyone who cries outside those hours is corrected.
Suggested line: There's something you should know about the man in the castle. He schedules grief: Thursdays, 3:00 to 3:05. Anyone who cries outside those hours is corrected.

Effective line: Thank you, a hundred times. We're at the plot every morning. What I told you is in your journal: he cannot stand a sadness he did not schedule.
Suggested line: Thank you, a hundred times over. I sit with him at the plot every morning now. Remember what I told you, it's in your journal: he can't bear a sadness he didn't schedule.

Effective line: Three wheels in the Transit Yards... three crews nobody ever told to stop. Pull their brake levers... take the foreman's whistle... tell them it's all right.
Suggested line: Three wheels in the Transit Yards... three crews nobody ever told to stop. Pull each brake lever... and tell them it's all right, in plain words.

Effective line: They won't believe you. Say it anyway. And cut the big cable by the east wall. The facade's lights have lived on my crews' legs for ten years.
Suggested line: They won't believe you at first... say it anyway. Then cut the big cable by the east wall. Those facade lights have run on my crews' legs... for ten years.

Effective line: Three wheels in the Transit Yards... free the crews. Cut the big cable by the east wall. Keep telling them they can stop.
Suggested line: Three wheels in the Transit Yards... free the crews, then cut the big cable by the east wall. Keep telling them they can stop... it takes a few goes.

Effective line: Heard the lights flicker from here. Heard the crews sit down. The whole yard... quiet.
Suggested line: I heard the lights flicker from here... then I heard the crews sit down. The whole yard's gone quiet.

Effective line: And something about him. He made lateness illegal. A man who cannot wait for anyone.
Suggested line: One thing about the man in the castle... he made lateness illegal. That's a man who can't bear to wait... for anyone.

Effective line: Wheels are slow. Crews are resting. What I said is in your journal: to him, lateness is disagreement, and disagreement is the one thing he won't forgive.
Suggested line: The wheels are slowing... and the crews are resting. Remember what I told you, it's in your journal: to him, lateness is disagreement... and that's the one thing he won't forgive.

Effective line: And the paste dispenser by the east wall: spoil it. Give it a very bad day.
Suggested line: And the paste dispenser here in the quarter: spoil it for me. Put something in it that tastes of something.

Effective line: Three recipe cards in the Hungry Quarter, and the dispenser to spoil. 'Some' of this, 'a bit' of that. Always a good recipe.
Suggested line: Three recipe cards in the Hungry Quarter, and the dispenser to spoil. You'll know my cards: 'some' of this, 'a bit' of that. That's how a good recipe reads.

Effective line: Look at the stains. Look at the spelling. And that smell from the dispenser: cabbage. Real cabbage.
Suggested line: Look at the stains on them, look at the spelling! And that smell from the dispenser... cabbage. Real cabbage.

Effective line: I am crying. Let me. Here: my real recipe, the one I never dared write down until today.
Suggested line: I'm crying, and you'll let me. Here: my real recipe, the one I never dared write down until today.

Effective line: And something about him. He cannot taste. Not food, not wine, not salt. He never could.
Suggested line: And one thing about the man in the castle: he can't taste. Not food, not wine, not salt. He never could.

Effective line: I'm cooking again. Real food, real mess. What I told you is in your journal: he made everyone eat what he could not taste.
Suggested line: I'm cooking again, real food with a real mess. Remember what I told you, it's in your journal: he made everyone eat what he couldn't taste.

Effective line: Three compost heaps are hiding in the Reek, in cellars and under floors, where they were told to wait. Rescue them. They're alive.
Suggested line: Three compost heaps are hiding in the Reek, in cellars and yards and under floors, where they were told to wait. Rescue them. They're alive, whatever the inspectors say.

Effective line: And there's an old seed in a jar somewhere nearby. Plant it in the Sick Patch, in the Reek. Nobody's planted a thing here in ten years.
Suggested line: And there's a jar of old seed somewhere in the Reek. Plant it in the Sick Patch. Nobody's planted a thing in this city for ten years.

Effective line: Three compost heaps and one jarred seed in the Reek. Rescue the heaps. Plant the seed in the Sick Patch. Give it a chance.
Suggested line: Three heaps to rescue in the Reek, and the seed for the Sick Patch. Find the jar first, then give the seed its chance. It's waited long enough.

Effective line: It took? It TOOK. A flower. In this city.
Suggested line: It took? It TOOK! A flower, in this city, after all this time.

Effective line: Here. Take it. And something about him: he's afraid of anything that grows without asking him first.
Suggested line: Here, take this. And one thing about the man in the castle: he's afraid of anything that grows without asking him first.

Effective line: Weeds. Moss. Children. Anything that surprises him. I think that's the whole of him.
Suggested line: Weeds, moss, children. Anything that might surprise him. I reckon that's the whole of him.

Effective line: Patch is blooming. Heaps are steaming. What I said is in your journal: he's afraid of anything that grows on its own.
Suggested line: The patch is blooming and the heaps are steaming, untidy as you like. Remember what I said, it's in your journal: he's afraid of anything that grows on its own.

Effective line: Good day! The weather is approved! The lawn is regulation!
Suggested line: Good day! The weather has been approved, and the lawn is exactly regulation!

Effective line: Good day! It is a very good day. It is the same day as yesterday.
Suggested line: Good day! It is a very good day, exactly the same as yesterday.

Effective line: The bread is lovely. The bread is... (a fixed smile) I have a permit for four more words. I wish it existed.
Suggested line: The bread is lovely. The bread is... (a fixed smile) I am only permitted to call it lovely. I would like, very much, to see some.

Effective line: I had a name before. I think it started with a B. I am allowed to forget it. I am doing very well at it.
Suggested line: I had a name before. I think it started with a B. We are allowed to forget them, and I am doing very well at it.

Effective line: Isn't it lovely to be exactly the same? I used to be different. I do not remember why. It sounds very tiring.
Suggested line: Isn't it lovely to be exactly the same? I used to be different, I think, though I cannot remember why. It sounds very tiring.

Effective line: Seventy percent, minimum! I am at seventy-one! It is a good day.
Suggested line: Seventy percent cheerfulness is the minimum, and today I am at seventy-one! It is a good day.

Effective line: The Showcase receives visitors from all over! (a pause) Nobody visits. Nobody has visited in six years. We still smile in case they do.
Suggested line: The Showcase receives visitors from all over! (a pause) Nobody has visited in six years. We still smile, in case they do.

Effective line: Do you hear the loudspeaker? It plays the same thing every day. It has said my name once.
Suggested line: Do you hear the loudspeaker? It says the same things every day, but once, years ago, it said my name.

Effective line: I tried to be spontaneous once. On a Tuesday. I said 'hello' to a bird.
Suggested line: I tried to be spontaneous once, on a Tuesday. I said 'hello' to a bird.

Effective line: Approved Hat Size: 1. I wear the one. It is a good hat. I do not know whose it is.
Suggested line: There is one Approved Hat Size, and this is the hat. It is a good hat, although I do not know whose it was.

Effective line: He is not here. He has never been here. The portraits are here.
Suggested line: He is never here, you know. He has never once come down. Only the portraits come.

Effective line: You try the front door. It does not open. It is not a door.
Suggested line: You try the front door, but it does not open, because it is not a door.

Effective line: It is a very well-painted rectangle on a wall. Somebody has painted a tiny brass knocker. You knock on it.
Suggested line: It is a very well-painted rectangle on the wall. Somebody has even painted a tiny brass knocker, so you knock.

Effective line: You try the door. It does not open. You peek through the window: it is a painting of a window, and beyond it a painting of a living room with a painting of a family.
Suggested line: The door will not open. Through the window you see a painting of a window, and beyond it a painted living room where a painted family sits.

Effective line: They are smiling. They have been smiling for six years.
Suggested line: They are all smiling, and they have been smiling for six years.

Effective line: The door has no handle. The house has no inside. Behind the facade there is just room for a ladder and a young woman painting the same window for the thousandth time.
Suggested line: The door has no handle, and the house has no inside. In the gap behind the facade there is just room for a ladder and a young woman painting the same window for the thousandth time.

Effective line: She looks at you. She looks away. She has the face of someone who has meant to write home for years.
Suggested line: She looks at you, then away. She has the face of someone who has meant to write home for years.

Effective line: You try the door. It is open! It is a closet.
Suggested line: You try the door, and to your surprise it opens. It is a closet.

Effective line: You can go in. You probably should not. Yet.
Suggested line: You could go in now. It would be wiser to wait until the city is back on its feet.

Effective line: The dispenser is spoiled. Lovely. But the paste comes from somewhere.
Suggested line: The dispenser's spoiled, and lovely it is too. But the paste has to come from somewhere, doesn't it?

Effective line: The shuttered stall at the south-west corner hums at night. Stalls are not supposed to hum. Open its ration hatch and look. Gently.
Suggested line: The shuttered stall at the quarter's south-west corner hums at night, and stalls don't hum. Open its ration hatch and have a look down. Gently.

Effective line: The south-west stall, the one with its shutter down. Open the ration hatch. Whatever is down there, it will be very, very grey.
Suggested line: It's the south-west stall, the one with its shutter down. Open the ration hatch, go down, and shut off whatever you find. I'd bet it's very, very grey.

Effective line: I have kept one real onion in my apron for ten years. Tonight, I chop it. You may want to stand back. I will be weeping, and not only from the onion.
Suggested line: I've kept one real onion in my apron for ten years, and tonight I'm chopping it. You may want to stand back. I'll be weeping, and not only from the onion.

Effective line: By the last energy wheel, a ferret in pinstripes is timing Rollo's crews. The crews are lying in the sun. She is still timing them.
Suggested line: By the last energy wheel, a ferret in pinstripes stands over Rollo's crews with a stopwatch. They are lying in the sun, and she is still timing them.

Effective line: Beside the Sick Patch, a hare in groundskeeper green is measuring Old Fern's seedling with a ruler. It is an inch over regulation. She has written that down.
Suggested line: Beside the Sick Patch, a hare in groundskeeper green is measuring Old Fern's seedling with a ruler. It is an inch over regulation, and she has written that down.

Effective line: Out of regulation. Everything is out of regulation now. The lawns, the hedges. They grow in whatever direction they like.
Suggested line: Out of regulation. Everything is out of regulation now, the lawns and the hedges both. They grow in whatever direction they please.

Effective line: Granny Gristle needs hands on the compost rows down in the Dump. Sorting peel from shell, all day. Messy. You'll hate it. Good.
Suggested line: Granny Gristle needs hands on the compost rows down in the Dump, sorting peel from shell all day long. It's messy work, and you'll hate it. Good.

Effective line: Just measuring. Lot of very tidy people in this city. Tidy is easy to measure.
Suggested line: Just measuring. There's a lot of very tidy people in this city, and tidy is easy to measure.

Effective line: Kestrel. I scout for the Wrinkles. Going into the city? There's an older way in than the gate. Follow the chalk, not the guards. The guards are worse at drawing.
Suggested line: Name's Kestrel. I scout for the Wrinkles. Heading into the city? There's an older way in than the gate. Follow my chalk, not the guards; they're worse at drawing.

Effective line: There's an older way into the city. Nobody remembers it. That's the point.
Suggested line: There's an older way into the city that nobody remembers. That's the whole point of it.

Effective line: Get inside and find the Crease: the manhole near the gate. Knock three times. Not two. Two is rude. Then ask Wren about the tunnels.
Suggested line: Get inside, then find the manhole near the gate and knock three times. Not two; two is rude. Wren's down in the Crease. Ask her about the tunnels.

Effective line: You found them. Told you I'd be here. Didn't say where. That's the fun part. Here, you've earned this.
Suggested line: So you found the Crease. Told you I'd be around; I just never said where. Here, you've earned this.

Effective line: You climb up past the walls. Nobody is watching this way in. Nobody remembers it. That is the point.
Suggested line: You climb up inside the walls. Nobody is watching this way in, because nobody remembers it is here.
